title: Several tasks at once
sub: One by one, WhenAll and WhenAny
cards/0/body:
A task starts at the moment the method is called: GetProfileAsync() sends the request right away and hands back a Task, and await only waits. So "start them together" means call all the methods first, then wait.

You can await three independent requests one by one: await, await, await. The times add up, because the next method is called only after the previous reply.

Or you can call all three at once and wait for them together with Task.WhenAll(…), a task that completes when all the tasks passed to it have completed. The time is that of the slowest request. If you pass tasks with a result, Task<T>, await WhenAll returns a T[] array in argument order.
cards/0/deep: Lazy Select. In var tasks = urls.Select(u => http.GetStringAsync(u)); no request has gone out yet: Select only describes a sequence. The requests start when WhenAll enumerates it. If you enumerate tasks again (say, tasks.Count() or a second WhenAll), the requests go out again. That's why people write .ToArray() or .ToList().
cards/1/task: Three requests: 300, 500 and 200 ms. Get the total time down to 500 ms or less.
cards/2/q: Three requests of 300, 500 and 200 ms are awaited one by one. How long does it all take?
cards/2/explain: 300 + 500 + 200. Each next method is called, and so its request starts, only after the previous reply.
cards/3/task: Go back to "one by one" and make the first request fail. What happened to the others?
cards/4/q: With sequential awaits, why did requests B and C never even start after A failed?
cards/4/options/0: await A threw, and execution never reached the lines with B and C
cards/4/explain: An exception stops the method at the very first await. GetOrdersAsync and GetBalanceAsync were never called, so their requests never started.
cards/5/body:
The WhenAll task completes only when all the tasks passed to it have completed, even if one of them failed right away.

If several failed, the WhenAll task ends faulted, and its Exception.InnerExceptions holds all the errors, in argument order, not in the order they happened. await throws the first one from that list (as in the previous lesson). To see them all, keep the WhenAll task in a variable.
cards/6/task: Switch to Task.WhenAll and make A and C fail (C, at 200 ms, fails before A). What does await throw, and what is stored in the WhenAll task?
cards/7/q: await Task.WhenAll(tA, tB, tC): A failed (at 300 ms) and C failed (at 200 ms, earlier). What does await throw?
cards/7/options/0: Only A's exception, the first in argument order
cards/7/options/1: Only C's exception, since it happened first
cards/7/explain: The errors in the WhenAll task are in argument order, and await throws the first one from the list: A's exception, even though C failed earlier. All the errors are in the WhenAll task's Exception.InnerExceptions. .Result and .Wait() would throw an AggregateException, not await.
cards/8/body:
Task.WhenAny returns a task that completes when the first of the given tasks completes, and its result is the winning task itself. Hence the double await: the first gets the winner, the second gets its result.

The winner is the first task to complete, including one that failed. WhenAny itself doesn't throw: the exception surfaces when you await the winner. The other tasks keep running, so you should cancel them with a token (next lesson).

The second example is a timeout: the work races against Task.Delay.
cards/9/q: You need data from whichever of three mirrors is fastest. What do you use?
cards/9/explain: WhenAny completes together with the fastest mirror. The other requests should be canceled with a token so they don't waste resources.
cards/10/q: The requests still go one by one. Which line is to blame?
cards/10/explain: The await inside the loop waits for each reply before the loop calls the next GetStringAsync. Remove that line: all the calls go out at once, and WhenAll waits for them all.
cards/11/q: Start all the requests at once
cards/11/explain: Every GetStringAsync is called before the waiting starts, so all the requests have gone out at once. WhenAll waits for all of them and returns the results array in url order.
